newsitem.title: UK: UK, Argentina to resume fishing talks.
newsitem.headline: UK, Argentina to resume fishing talks.

text.p: Britain and Argentina have agreed to restart negotiations on the vexed question of fishing rights in disputed waters of the South Atlantic, British officials said on Monday.
They said the decision was taken during informal talks near London at the weekend between Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and his Argentine counterpart Guido Di Tella.
"There will be a new effort on the idea of a long-term fisheries agreement," one senior official said.
He said no date had been set for the talks, which would be held at the level of senior officials, not ministers.
Britain and Argentina fought a brief but bloody war over the disputed Falkland Islands in 1982.
The two countries have since restored full diplomatic relations and in 1995 signed a deal to explore for oil in waters around the Falklands, which Argentina calls the Malvinas.

But fishing rights and conservation plans have been a bone of contention, and Britain last spring sent a destroyer to South Georgia, a British territory 800 miles (1,480 km) southeast of the Falklands, to enforce current fisheries legislation.
Low-level contacts since then have made little progress and British officials cautioned against a quick breakthrough, saying the issue remained very tricky.
The Falklands, and general Anglo-Argentine ties, dominated the Rifkind-Di Tella talks, which a Foreign Office spokesman described as wide-ranging and informal.
Britain reaffirmed its position before the talks began that there could be no question of its offering to share or transfer sovereignty of the islands to Argentina.
